title: Brutal Thanksgiving Storms Batter U.S. with Record Snow, 65 MPH Winds, and Widespread Travel Chaos
snippet: A massive multi-front holiday storm knocked out power to hundreds of thousands of Americans, grounded thousands of flights, and forced an unprecedented delay of the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade.
content:
Millions of Americans celebrating Thanksgiving faced a chaotic holiday as a series of powerful storms slammed the nation, triggering widespread power outages, severe travel disruptions, and unprecedented event delays from the Midwest to the East Coast.

Forecasters from the National Weather Service warned that hazardous conditions, driven by torrential rain, damaging wind gusts, and heavy snow, would persist through late November across the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast. The extreme weather battered critical infrastructure and left over 800,000 customers without electricity by Thursday night, with the heaviest outages concentrated in coastal Virginia, Maryland, and the St. Louis metropolitan area.

Parade Postponed and Emergency Declarations

In New York, Governor Kathy Hochul issued a preemptive state of emergency for New York City and surrounding suburban counties as wind gusts threatened to reach up to 65 mph. The dangerous sustained winds forced organizers to take the rare step of rescheduling the iconic Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade to November 28, citing safety concerns for crowd safety and balloon handlers. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani urged residents to remain indoors, warning that the intense gusts could easily down tree limbs and power lines.

Historic Midwest Snowfall and Structural Damage

While coastal areas grappled with high winds and street flooding, parts of the Midwest were blanketed by historic holiday snowfall. Southeastern Missouri saw up to 14 inches of snow, with Columbia recording its heaviest Thanksgiving snowstorm in nearly five decades. St. Louis logged over seven inches of snow—marking the first time in recorded history the city reported top-ten November snowfalls in consecutive years. The weight of the heavy snow led to the collapse of the Wentzville Ice Arena northwest of St. Louis, forcing its closure until further notice.

Travel Nightmares and Infrastructure Strains

Holiday travel ground to a near-halt in several major hubs. FlightAware reported over 2,200 delays and more than 1,200 cancellations for U.S. flights on Thursday, with Baltimore/Washington International Airport, JFK, Boston Logan, and Washington Dulles bearing the brunt of the disruptions.

Infrastructure struggled under the storm's weight elsewhere as well. In Maryland, state officials shut down the Chesapeake Bay Bridge in both directions due to severe winds. Nearby, the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission requested nearly two million residents in Montgomery and Prince George's counties to immediately restrict water usage to essential needs after power supply disruptions threatened local filtration plants.

Severe Conditions Coast to Coast

The weather mayhem extended all the way to the West Coast. In the Pacific Northwest, NWS Seattle issued tornado warnings and landspout alerts for communities southeast of the city. Meanwhile, northern California experienced dangerous high surf and sneaker waves up to 19 feet, leading to localized coastal flooding and causing structural damage to the Pacifica Pier near San Francisco.
